result.proved: A thin contour around the fully resolved radial critical-value star has full-cycle monodromy but average complete-lift length at least 2 sum_c L(c)/k. If every pairwise root chord exceeds k/(k-1), that lower bound exceeds two. Generic normalized cubic and quartic examples satisfying the criterion exist near the regular triangle and square.
result.human_understanding_delta: Fixed-point-free monodromy is topologically easy for the resolved critical tree, but that construction double-charges every critical edge. The hard near-regular regime therefore requires cluster-aware monodromy geometry, not merely a derangement permutation.
result.verification_state: PASS ordinary exact proof; PASS exhaustive finite permutation replay through degree six; PASS exact rational squared inequalities for the cubic and quartic margins
result.lean_scope: No Lean theorem was added: the load-bearing new step is a planar covering/length-liminf argument, while the finite permutation and scalar kernels are replayed exactly by the checker. Formalizing only the scalar inequalities would displace proof search without strengthening authority.
result.claim_boundary: This rules out only lollipops obtained by separately resolving every critical value with radial slits and circling the entire slit star. It does not rule out grouped critical-value contours, fixed safe moved blocks, fixed-sheet compensation, componentwise combined charge, COVER, FP--GM, or Erdős 1041.
result.surviving_frontier: Construct a cluster-aware loop that charges a near-coincident critical-value group once while retaining a moved-sheet average complete-lift bound at most two.
